_README: Contract breaches the read-only integration suite commits when replayed
against the fake. This is a RATCHET, asserted exactly: a NEW entry fails
CI, and so does a STALE one, so a fix has to be recorded here as well.
Every entry is a call the suite makes that the endpoint catalog
(tests/endpoints.json) does not support. Against a live Ghidra each one
still returns HTTP 200 -- the plugin ignores parameters it does not
declare -- so the test passes while asserting nothing about the thing its
name claims. That is why they were invisible until an offline run had a
None of these are fixed here on purpose. Changing what a test asserts is
a maintainer decision, and two of them arguably want deleting rather than
repairing. Recording them is what stops them being forgotten again.
Discovered by W12 / issue #112, 2026-08-30, against tests/endpoints.json

violations.note: /disassemble_bytes is a POST endpoint. The test GETs it and accepts [200, 404], so it passes on the 404 a live server returns -- while proving nothing about disassembly.
Not in the catalog. The test already accepts [200, 404] and its own comment says 'may not exist - use decompile_function instead', so it is a permanently-404 no-op.
Not in the catalog. Same permanently-404 shape as /get_decompiled_code; /disassemble_function is the real endpoint.
Not in the catalog. The catalogued endpoint is /list_scripts (param: filter).
The declared parameter is `function_address`, not `address`. Sent as `address` it is dropped, so the endpoint scores whatever the server's current function is -- and the test asserts only status 200.
Declared parameters are format, limit, program. `max_depth` is silently ignored, so the test does not exercise depth limiting at all.

/list_functions is documented in ListingService.java as 'List all functions (no pagination)' and declares only `program`. test_list_functions_with_limit therefore tests a capability the endpoint does not have and can never fail.
Same as [limit]. The test is named for pagination the endpoint does not implement.
The declared parameter is `name_pattern`. Sent as `pattern` the filter is dropped entirely, so the call returns an unfiltered listing and the test asserts only status 200.
